## EMST role: Hydrologist (state variant, journey level; P2)

*Match:* `skos:closeMatch`, confidence 0.6, unreviewed agent draft (`emst-x5-tx:R17-hydrologist/state:2460`). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

**Competency targets at this level (agent draft)**

- Plan water supply and allocation under hydrologic uncertainty — journey L2 *(distinguishing)*
- Characterize groundwater systems and protect drinking water sources — journey L2
- Build, calibrate and validate predictive and simulation models of environmental systems — journey L2
- Quantify and communicate uncertainty for environmental decisions — journey L2
- Assess stream channel form and function in the field — journey L2
- Analyze environmental data statistically and interpret the results — journey L2
- Measure water quality and survey aquatic communities in the field — journey L2
- Develop pollutant load allocations and watershed restoration plans for impaired waters — journey L2
- Use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work — journey L1
- Evaluate model fitness-for-purpose and validate against independent evidence — journey L2
- Validate AI-generated work products before professional use — journey L1
- Deploy, maintain and verify field sensor networks — journey L2
- Analyze and interpret climate observations and projections for management decisions — journey L2

**Main tasks at this level (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- Prepare a drought contingency plan with triggers, stages and response actions tied to supply indicators — 5.1% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Run an aquifer test on a supply well or wellfield to estimate transmissivity and storage from drawdown and recovery data — 5.1% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Delineate a wellhead or source-water protection area from hydrogeologic data and time-of-travel criteria — 5.1% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Simulate ecosystem response to alternative land-use and climate scenarios, documenting scenario assumptions and the sensitivity of results to each. — 5.1% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Forecast water demand and supply under drought and climate scenarios for a utility or basin plan, stating assumptions and uncertainty — 4.1% *(critical, needed at entry)*
- Compare conjunctive-use, reuse and storage options by yield, cost and reliability for an integrated resource plan — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Review a well construction or injection well application against construction and protection standards before approval — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Build a predictive model of fire risk, pest outbreak or water availability, validating it on years or areas withheld from fitting. — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Forecast resource management needs from a validated predictive model, stating the horizon and interval for each estimate. — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Survey channel cross-sections, longitudinal profile and substrate at a reach following the geomorphic assessment protocol — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Identify bankfull indicators and channel evolution stage at a reach from field evidence — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
- Collect grab water samples at locations and depths that represent the condition of interest, recording flow and site conditions at collection — 4.1% *(needed at entry)*
